extracted.intended_audience: parties, potential parties, interested governmental participants, deponents, and counsel participating in NRC adjudicatory proceedings (license applicants, intervenors, and NRC staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedural rules governing discovery, prehearing conferences, schedules, motions, hybrid and simplified hearing procedures, and the roles/responsibilities of parties and NRC staff in NRC adjudications (10 CFR Part 2, selected sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded materials from initial electronic availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The following material is excluded from the initial requirements of §2.1003 to be made available electronically, but is subject to derivative discovery under paragraph (i)(1) of this section—(i) Personal records; (ii) Travel vouchers; (iii) Speeches; (iv) Preliminary drafts; (v) Marginalia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories of documents need not be included in initial electronic production, but remain subject to derivative discovery; identical documents modified or with notations are treated as separate documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for paper copies from deponent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party or interested governmental participant may request from the deponent a paper copy of any or all of the documents on the index that have not already been provided electronically (subject to paragraph (i)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for paper copies are permitted even when electronic production is the norm; subject to limitations set in the referenced paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deponent obligation to bring or submit paper copies for depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The deponent shall bring a paper copy of all documents on the index that the deposing party requests that have not already been provided electronically to an oral deposition, or submit such documents with the certified deposition for depositions taken on written questions (subject to paragraph (i)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures availability of documentary materials at deposition when electronic copies have not been provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to make index documents electronically available for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party or interested governmental participant may request that any or all documents on the index that have not already been provided electronically, and on which it intends to rely at hearing, be made electronically available by the deponent (subject to paragraph (i)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows parties to insist on electronic availability of materials they intend to rely on at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility when deposing non-party or non-interest participant
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposing party or interested governmental participant shall assume the responsibility for the obligations set forth in paragraphs (i)(1), (i)(3), (i)(4), and (i)(5) when deposing someone other than a party or interested governmental participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places burden for fulfilling electronic/paper production obligations on the deposing party when the deponent is not a party/interested governmental participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry upon land inspection request
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party, potential party, or interested governmental participant may serve a request to permit entry upon designated land or other property in the possession or control of the requestee for access to raw data, inspection and measuring, surveying, photographing, testing, or sampling the property or any designated object or operation thereon, within the scope of §2.1018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits on-site inspections and related activities; see related scope limitations in §2.1018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of inspection request without leave
rubrics_metrics.description: The request may be served on any party, potential party, or interested governmental participant without leave of the Commission or the Presiding Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No advance court/Presiding Officer permission required to serve an entry inspection request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description standard for inspection requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall describe with reasonable particularity the land or other property to be inspected either by individual item or by category, and shall specify a reasonable time, place, and manner of making the inspection and performing the related acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be sufficiently specific (particularity) and propose reasonable logistics for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and content to inspection request
rubrics_metrics.description: The party upon whom the request is served shall serve a written response within ten days after service. The response shall state, with respect to each item or category, that inspection and related activities will be permitted as requested, unless the request is objected to, in which case the reasons for objection shall be stated; if objection made to part of an item or category, the part shall be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses with specific grounds for objection are required; partial objections must be particularized.

rubrics_metrics.name: First prehearing conference timing and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: In specified proceedings (e.g., HLW repository construction authorization or license to receive/possess HLW), the Commission or presiding officer will direct parties to appear within seventy days after notice of hearing, or such other time as appropriate, for a conference to: (1) Permit identification of the key issues; (2) Take steps necessary for further identification of the issues; (3) Consider all intervention petitions; (4) Establish a schedule for further actions; and (5) Establish a discovery schedule taking into account the objective of meeting the three-year time schedule specified in section 114(d) of the NWPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early conference to narrow issues, consider interventions, and set schedules including discovery consistent with statutory timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to order further conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer may order any further formal and informal conferences among the parties and interested governmental participants including teleconferences, to the extent that it considers that such a conference would expedite the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding Officer can require additional meetings to promote efficient case management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference stenographic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A prehearing conference held pursuant to this section shall be stenographically reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an official record of prehearing conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference order contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer shall enter an order which recites the action taken at the conference, the schedule for further actions in the proceeding, and any agreements by the parties, and which identifies key issues, makes preliminary or final determinations as to parties and interested governmental participants, and provides for submission of status reports on discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizes conference outcomes and sets expectations for future procedures and discovery reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second prehearing conference timing and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: In specified HLW proceedings the Commission or presiding officer shall direct parties to appear not later than thirty days after the Safety Evaluation Report is issued for a conference to consider: (1) Any amended contentions (to be reviewed under §2.309(c)); (2) Simplification and specification of issues; (3) Obtaining stipulations and admissions of fact and of contents/authenticity of documents; (4) Identification of witnesses and limitation of expert witnesses; (5) Setting a hearing schedule; (6) Establishing a discovery schedule consistent with the three-year objective; and (7) Other matters to aid orderly disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second conference focuses on narrowing and preparing evidentiary presentation and limiting experts to expedite hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second prehearing conference order
rubrics_metrics.description: A prehearing conference held pursuant to this section shall be stenographically reported and the Presiding Officer shall enter an order reciting action taken, agreements by the parties, limits the issues or defines matters in controversy, and sets discovery and hearing schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry of formal order to memorialize narrowing of issues and schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness of favorable initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending review and final decision by the Commission, an initial decision resolving all issues before the presiding officer in favor of issuance or amendment of either an authorization to construct a HLW repository or a license to receive and possess HLW will be immediately effective upon issuance except as provided in any order issued in accordance with §2.342 that stays effectiveness, or as otherwise provided by the Commission in special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial favorable decisions take effect immediately unless stayed or other special Commission action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director issuance of authorization/license after initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards shall promptly issue a construction authorization or license, notwithstanding filing/pendency of appeal, following an initial decision resolving all issues in favor of licensing upon making appropriate licensing findings, except as provided in paragraph (c) or orders under §2.342 or special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must act promptly to issue license after initial decision unless Commission supervisory/review steps or stays apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission supervisory examination of contested issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the Director may issue a construction authorization or license, the Commission shall undertake and complete a supervisory examination of contested issues to consider whether there is any significant basis for doubting that the facility will be constructed or operated with adequate protection of public health and safety, and whether the Commission should suspend or otherwise condition effectiveness of Presiding Officer decision. This supervisory examination is not part of the adjudicatory proceeding. The Commission shall notify the Director in writing when completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate Commission-level safety/protection review can suspend issuance; it is outside the adjudicatory record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review of uncontested issues required for licensing findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the Director issues authorization or license, the Commission shall review those issues not contested in the proceeding but about which the Director must make findings prior to issuance; Director shall issue only after written notification from Commission that its review is complete and issuance is appropriate. This Commission review is not part of adjudicatory proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Commission oversight of uncontested matters necessary for licensing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/postponement of effectiveness must be written and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: No suspension of the effectiveness of a Presiding Officer's initial decision or postponement of the Director's issuance resulting from a Commission supervisory examination or review will be entered except in writing with a statement of the reasons. Such suspension or postponement will be limited to such period as is necessary for the Commission to resolve the matters at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires written reasons and temporal limitation when Commission pauses effectiveness of Presiding Officer decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure following supervisory examination suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the supervisory examination results in a suspension of effectiveness under paragraph (c)(1), the Commission will take review sua sponte and further proceedings relative to contested matters will be in accordance with procedures for participation by the DOE, the NRC staff, or other parties and interested governmental participants as established by the Commission in its written statement of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out that suspension triggers Commission review with appropriate participation procedures described in a written statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on use of motions for decision in geologic repository proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding involving a construction authorization for a geologic repository operations area, the procedure for decision on the pleadings may be used only for determination of specific subordinate issues and may not be used to determine the ultimate issue as to whether the authorization must be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts summary disposition for ultimate licensing question in geologic repository matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for decision on pleadings: filing and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may move, with or without supporting affidavits, for a decision by the Presiding Officer as to all or any part of the matters. The moving party shall annex a separate, short, and concise statement of the material facts as to which it contends there is no genuine issue. Motions may be filed at any time. Any other party may file an answer supporting or opposing within 20 days, and shall annex a separate short and concise statement of material facts it contends present genuine issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material facts in the moving party's statement deemed admitted unless controverted; procedural deadlines apply; the Presiding Officer may dismiss or hold motions filed shortly before hearing if they would divert substantial resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit standards in support/opposition to motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits must set forth those facts that would be admissible in evidence and show affirmatively that the affiant is competent to testify. The Presiding Officer may permit affidavits to be supplemented or opposed by further affidavits. Opposing parties must set forth specific facts showing a genuine issue; cannot rest on mere allegations or denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits must meet evidentiary competence and admissibility standards; failure to present specific rebuttal facts permits decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting motion for summary decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer shall render the decision sought if the filings show that there is no genuine issue as to any material fact and that the moving party is entitled to a decision as a matter of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic summary judgment standard applied in adjudicatory context, with special limitations for geologic repository cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to appendix D schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraphs (b) and (c), the Presiding Officer shall adhere to the schedule set forth in appendix D of this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary scheduling framework is appendix D; exceptions limited per following paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short extension authority for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to §2.307, the Presiding Officer may approve extensions of no more than fifteen (15) days beyond any required time set forth in this subpart for a filing by a party. Except in exceptional/unforeseen circumstances, requests for extensions of more than fifteen (15) days must be filed no later than five (5) days in advance of the required time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding Officer can grant short extensions; longer ones require timely advance filing and referral to Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions beyond 15 days referred to Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions beyond 15 days must be referred to the Commission. If the Commission does not disapprove the extension within 10 days of receiving the request, the extension will be effective. If the Commission disapproves, the date in question will be set for 5 days after the Commission's disapproval action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Silence from Commission within 10 days equals approval by default; disapproval triggers a short reset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding Officer delay in issuing orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer may delay the issuance of an order up to thirty days beyond the time set forth in appendix D. If the Presiding Officer anticipates issuance later than the thirty-day extension, they shall notify the Commission at least ten days in advance of the scheduled milestone and provide justification for the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits and notice requirements for Presiding Officer delays beyond schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sua sponte limitation on findings in HLW-related initial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: In any initial decision in a proceeding on an application for a construction authorization or a license to receive and possess HLW at a geologic repository operations area, the Presiding Officer, other than the Commission, shall make findings of fact and conclusions of law on, and otherwise give consideration to, only those matters put into controversy by the parties and determined to be litigable issues in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents Presiding Officer from raising or deciding issues on their own initiative in specified HLW proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Subpart K (hybrid hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations in this subpart establish hybrid hearing procedures, as authorized by section 134 of the NWPA, to be used at the request of any party in certain contested proceedings on applications for a license or license amendment to expand spent nuclear fuel storage capacity at civilian nuclear power plant sites. These procedures are intended to encourage and expedite onsite expansion of spent nuclear fuel storage capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart K provides an alternative/hybrid hearing track intended to speed certain spent fuel storage expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart K
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart, together with subpart C and applicable provisions of subparts G and L, govern adjudicatory proceedings on applications filed after Jan 7, 1983, for licenses or amendments to expand spent fuel storage capacity under parts 50 or 53, or for licenses under part 72 for ISFSIs at reactor sites. It does not apply to the first application at a site using a new technology not previously approved, nor to license transfer proceedings (Subpart M applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the universe of cases eligible for hybrid procedures and important exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed action must identify hybrid procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For eligible applications, the Commission will publish in the Federal Register a notice of proposed action in accordance with §2.105 that will identify the availability of the hybrid hearing procedures, specify that any party may invoke these procedures by filing a timely request for oral argument under §2.1109, and state that if oral argument is granted any hearing will be conducted under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice must inform parties of availability and invocation route for hybrid procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request oral argument to invoke hybrid procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In its request for hearing/petition to intervene or in the applicant's or NRC staff's response, any party may invoke the hybrid hearing procedures by requesting an oral argument. If it is determined a hearing will be held, the presiding officer shall grant a timely request. Untimely requests may be granted for good cause after opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral argument request is the mechanism to invoke hybrid procedures; timeliness and good cause standards apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding Officer order on oral argument requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall issue a written order ruling on any requests for oral argument. If granted, the order shall include a schedule for discovery and subsequent oral argument with respect to the admitted contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting oral argument triggers an explicit discovery/oral-argument schedule in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback if no oral argument requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If no party requests oral argument, or if all untimely requests are denied, the presiding officer shall conduct the proceeding in accordance with the subpart under which the proceeding was initially conducted as determined in accordance with §2.310.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default procedural track applies unless oral argument is timely granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument filing requirements (25-day summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty-five (25) days prior to oral argument, each party shall submit to the presiding officer a detailed written summary of all facts, data, and arguments known to the party and on which it proposes to rely at oral argument, and shall submit supporting facts and data in the form of sworn written testimony or other sworn written submission; materials must be simultaneously served on all other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires pre-argument disclosure of the factual and evidentiary basis in sworn form to all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument reply (10 days) and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten (10) days prior to oral argument, each party may submit a reply limited to addressing whether the written summaries, facts, data, and arguments filed under paragraph (a) support or refute the existence of a genuine and substantial dispute of fact. Replies must be simultaneously served on all other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies are narrowly focused on whether submissions establish a genuine and substantial dispute of fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only sworn written testimony admissible at oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Only facts and data in the form of sworn written testimony or other sworn written submission may be relied on by the parties during oral argument, and the presiding officer shall consider those facts and data only if they are submitted in that form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits reliance on unsworn factual assertions at oral argument; enforces evidentiary formality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of issues for adjudicatory hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: After consideration of oral presentation and written facts/data, the presiding officer shall promptly by written order: (1) Designate any disputed issues of fact and remaining issues of law for resolution in an adjudicatory hearing; and (2) Dispose of any issues of law or fact not designated for resolution. For each designated issue, the presiding officer shall identify specific facts in genuine and substantial dispute, why Commission decision likely depends on resolution, and why adjudicatory hearing likely to resolve the dispute. If no disputed issues, the presiding officer shall dismiss the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit statement of factual disputes and their materiality is required to take an issue to hearing; non-designated issues get a reasoned disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for designating issues (§2.1115(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: No issue shall be designated for resolution in an adjudicatory hearing unless the presiding officer determines that: (1) There is a genuine and substantial dispute of fact which can only be resolved with sufficient accuracy by introduction of evidence in an adjudicatory hearing; and (2) The decision of the Commission is likely to depend in whole or in part on the resolution of that dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-prong test—genuine/substantial dispute and materiality to Commission decision—required to justify hearing designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from consideration when designating issues
rubrics_metrics.description: In making a determination under paragraph (b), the presiding officer shall not consider: (1) Any issue relating to the design, construction, or operation of any civilian nuclear power reactor already licensed at the site, unless the presiding officer determines such issue substantially affects the design/construction/operation of the facility/activity at issue; or (2) Any siting or design issue fully considered and decided by the Commission in connection with issuance of a construction permit or operating license for the reactor at that site, unless revision of siting/design criteria occurred and presiding officer determines substantial effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents relitigation of matters already decided unless new criteria or substantial effects are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeals of issue-designation orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the presiding officer disposes of all issues and dismisses the proceeding, appeals from the presiding officer's order disposing of issues and designating one or more issues for adjudicatory hearing are interlocutory and must await the end of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits immediate appellate review of issue-designation orders to avoid piecemeal appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant bears the ultimate burden of proof (risk of non-persuasion) with respect to the contention in the proceeding. The proponent of the request for an adjudicatory hearing bears the burden of demonstrating under §2.1115(b) that an adjudicatory hearing should be held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates burdens: (a) establishing need for hearing (proponent), and (b) ultimate proof at hearing (applicant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of other subparts
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings subject to this part, the provisions of subparts A, C, and L of this part are also applicable, except where inconsistent with provisions of this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to other procedural rules; note that inconsistencies control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart L (Simplified Hearing Procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this subpart, together with subpart C of this part, govern adjudicatory proceedings conducted for the grant, renewal, licensee-initiated amendment, or termination of licenses or permits subject to various listed parts (parts 30, 32–36, 39, 40, 50, 52, 53, 54, 55, 61, 70, and 72), except as determined through application of §2.310(b)–(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines where simplified procedures apply across a broad swath of NRC licensing actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: applicability of §2.4
rubrics_metrics.description: The definitions of terms contained in §2.4 apply to this subpart unless a different definition is provided in this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard definitional cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff authority and role during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: During any hearing under this subpart, consistent with NRC staff's findings in its review and as authorized by law, the NRC staff is expected to promptly issue its approval or denial of the application, or take other appropriate action on the underlying regulatory matter. When the staff takes its action, it must notify the presiding officer and parties and include explanation why public health and safety is protected and why action is in accord with common defense and security. The staff's action is effective upon issuance except in enumerated matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff may act administratively during pendency; must explain safety/security rationale and notify parties/presiding officer; certain high-significance matters are excepted from immediate effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances where staff action is not effective upon issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff action on the matter is effective upon issuance by the staff, except in matters involving: (1) Applications to construct/operate production or utilization facilities (including limited work authorizations and combined licenses under specified parts); (2) Early site permits; (3) Manufacturing licenses under specified parts; (4) Amendments to construction authorizations for HLW repositories under specified rules; (5) Applications for ISFSI at non-reactor sites under part 72; and (6) licensing actions that involve significant hazards considerations as defined in specified sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates important categories where staff cannot make effective action while adjudication is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: When NRC staff must participate as a party
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC staff is not required to be a party to a proceeding under this subpart, except where: (i) The proceeding involves an application denied by the NRC staff or an enforcement action proposed by the NRC staff; or (ii) The presiding officer determines staff participation would materially aid resolution and orders staff to participate for identified issues. If necessary, the presiding officer shall issue an order identifying the issues and basis for staff participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff participation as a party is discretionary except in certain scenarios and when ordered for material assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff notice to participate and disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days of issuance of the order granting requests for hearing/petitions to intervene and admitting contentions, the NRC staff shall notify the presiding officer and the parties whether it desires to participate as a party and identify the contentions on which it wishes to participate. If it desires to participate thereafter, it shall notify and make disclosures required by §2.336(b)(3)–(5) unless accompanying an affidavit explaining why disclosures cannot be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notice and disclosure obligations apply if staff elects party status; staff assumes party rights/responsibilities upon choosing to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing file creation and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the order granting requests for hearing/petitions to intervene and admitting contentions, the NRC staff shall file in the docket, present to the presiding officer, and make available to the parties a hearing file, either by hard copies or on the NRC Web site. The hearing file also must be made available for public inspection/copying at the NRC Web site and/or the NRC Public Document Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties and public have access to core documentary bases for the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the hearing file
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing file consists of the application and amendments, and, when available, any NRC environmental impact statement or assessment and any NRC report related to the proposed action, as well as any correspondence between the applicant/licensee and the NRC that is relevant to the proposed action. Documents already available at the NRC website or Public Document Room may be incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding Officer rules on what materials are appropriate for the hearing file; file must be kept current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on party discovery from NRC or other parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise permitted by subpart C, a party may not seek discovery from any other party or the NRC or its personnel, whether by document production, deposition, interrogatories or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplified procedures sharply limit conventional inter-party discovery; consult subpart C exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions and requests general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings under this subpart, requirements for motions and requests and responses are as specified in §2.323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to general motion practice standards in §2.323.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for motions requesting cross-examination by parties
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a motion to permit cross-examination by the parties on particular admitted contentions or issues, accompanied by a cross-examination plan containing: (i) a brief description of the issue(s); (ii) the objective to be achieved by cross-examination; and (iii) the proposed line of questions that may logically lead to achieving the objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination requests must be planned and justified in advance with a logical question plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment and later disclosure of cross-examination plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The cross-examination plan may be submitted only to the presiding officer and must be kept by the presiding officer in confidence until issuance of the initial decision on the issue being litigated. The presiding officer shall then provide each cross-examination plan to the Commission's Secretary for inclusion in the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects tactical plans during litigation but preserves them for the official record at decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for allowing party cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall allow cross-examination by the parties only if the presiding officer determines that cross-examination by the parties is necessary to ensure the development of an adequate record for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination by parties is discretionary and tied to record adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary disposition timing and requirements (Subpart L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for summary disposition may be submitted to the presiding officer by any party no later than 45 days before the commencement of hearing. Motions must be in writing and include a written explanation of the basis and a short concise statement of material facts contended to have no genuine issue. Served on parties and Secretary. Other parties may answer within 20 days. The presiding officer shall issue determination no later than 15 days before hearing and shall apply standards set forth in subpart G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timing and content rules for summary disposition motions to preserve hearing preparation time and permit rulings before hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal hearings: written-submission alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings under this subpart will be oral unless, within 15 days of service of the order granting the request for hearing, the parties unanimously agree and file a joint motion requesting a hearing consisting of written submissions. A motion to hold a hearing consisting of written submissions will not be entertained unless there is unanimous consent of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unanimous party agreement is required to convert to a written-submissions hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and schedule for oral hearing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants in an oral hearing may submit and sponsor: (1) Initial written statements of position and written testimony with supporting affidavits on admitted contentions, filed on dates set by the presiding officer; (2) Written responses and rebuttal testimony with supporting affidavits directed to initial statements, filed within 20 days of service of initial materials unless presiding officer directs otherwise; (3) Proposed questions for the presiding officer to consider for propounding to the persons sponsoring the testimony, received no later than 20 days after initial materials (or no later than 5 days before hearing if shorter timeframe), and proposed questions need not be filed with any other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed schedule for exchange of testimony, rebuttal, and proposed questions to structure oral hearings and ensure timely preparation.
